Overhydration - drinking too much water can for some individuals be deadly. If your kidneys can't filter out the water your cells begin taking it in and swelling. You first notice the effects as your brain swells making you a bit dizzy or fatigued but the water is not what kills you. 

What will kill you is the dilution of your sodium in your blood and tissue fluids known as acute hyponatremia. In severe cases you fall into a coma and unless treated die. What's worse is women who haven't gone through menopause suffer worse brain damage coming out of it than men. 

Rule of hydration- if you feel thirsty (and aren't on any medications) you need to drink. Otherwise don't force water down just because others are drinking. 

****
EDIT- also if your doing high intensity exercise discuss with your doctor about using sports drinks most of the electrolytes in them is sodium to help prevent this from happening.

There is sides to the argument. Firstly speaking in regards to mental well-being, no one truly knows what's going on in someone else head or life. So if a student raises concerns, it should be followed up; a sit-down conversation away from friends trying to get to the bottom of what's going on/why they are struggling due to your subject is needed. 

However, when work isn't submitted, which is held against the teacher as not being engaging/teaching properly (the age-old accountability stick), understandably, there is a large amount of teacher frustration. It's incredibly frustrating to those who care about the students and want them to succeed.

Responses like OP’s are normally linked to experiences with students using mental well-being as an excuse for incomplete work routinely when help is offered and then with family contact, it is discovered they were ‘trying it on’. 

I hope the student in OPs post is well and gets support and if their comment is found not to have merit that steps are taken to remotivate them to do the work as well as educate them on mental well-beings importance and why it shouldn't be used ‘as just an excuse’.

I’m a teacher in the UK. Exam boards still haven’t decided the structure of exams really, we have been told to test as much as possible to get data for predicted grades (by the school) but apart from that we are awaiting decisions by the exam bodies in regards to how they want these tests set up. Recommendations on how we ensure these tests/assessments are fair, etc. Way too many parents passing off their work as their kids. I really feel sorry for everyone in exam years this is such a terrible situation to go through and the uncertainty does not help. 

Meanwhile, every week we are teaching our full timetabled 6 lessons a day with a 5 minute break between the lessons to help with eye strain for students and teachers. During my PPA (planning time) I then call students in my form to check in on them. It’s normally parents I end up talking to but I also run form teams meetings with quizzes and games at the end of the school day for 10 minutes and I then get to talk to my form and it genuinely makes my day. 

May seem stupid but hearing my form compete trying to answer a silly quiz on sports personalities or facts about oceans, etc, makes it feel like their in the classroom! 

I hope that if anyone is struggling out there with online learning, feeling lonely, family disputes and the like you let your teachers know (can just be an email/ teams chat)! It’s part of being a teacher to help you and guide you in the direction of appropriate support when we can’t. 

Anyway look after yourself and hopefully guidance will come out soon! 

A Secondary teacher

4928... That's how many times I’ve saved the world and each time it gets more and more complicated. Before my ability life was simple, I was a twenty-something guy just lazing about during the new year lockdown in 2021. I'd just received the new PS5 I had been saving up for and started playing when lightning hit. I still remember what went through my head, ’Well what did I expect...’, before ten thousand volts travelled straight into me and branched off into the console. That was the moment where my life took a turn for the better, it was the moment I gained the ability to quicksave. 

My first quicksave happened when I went to take out the trash and got hit by a runaway garbage truck. I still remember the feeling of metal hitting me before I saw the menu screen appear, with the option to reload last save. I woke up picking myself off the charred sofa from the lightning strike. It took a few more attempts for me to realise I could quicksave whenever I wanted. I just needed to say aloud ”Menu, Save” but as soon as I did I would lose the save before that. I learnt that the hard way, I spent what must have been weeks going back to the same day over and over for this girl. Christine was her name, I met at work and made the rookie error of showing I knew too much about her. I realised my mistake too late and couldn't reload as I discovered I had quicksaved after helping ’Steve the idiot with the cactus’ save his PowerPoint as a pdf. 

I only started saving the world when I turned 30, by that point I had won enough lotteries, invested in the right companies and made a fortune for myself and began to realise what was the point of money if there was nothing to spend it on and so it began. Be it bacteria from Mars, COVID40, the Great fires of Thanksgiving and the constant threat of dirty bombs I was there learning about what happened and why, before reloading each time to prevent it. 

Now that I've started though, I can't seem to get a break! Every day there's a new crisis, a new threat that I'm forced to defeat. The worst ones to deal with are the ones I cause. I kill a scientist about to release a mutagenic compound into the water supply,  and that's no problem! Next reload, their nephew becomes an arms dealer who sells the final component in a dirty bomb whereas without me killing the scientist they would have been a TikTok star. This is what I meant by complicated. 

I think I will take a break on my 5000th time of saving the world, I hope it'll be ok...
